notes: SHIP v1.14.464 - THE BUILD BANNER STACK IS RETIRED, AND THREE TOOLS THAT HAD NO DOOR COME BACK. OWNER RULING 2026-08-19: #bw-shell replaced the banner landing, fold the stack. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, because it is worse than redundancy. bw_render adds bw-on to #pg-work in all three of its routing branches and nothing in the file ever removed it, and it runs on every showMode('work'). So body.rd #pg-work.bw-on #work-grid was display:none from the first Work visit onward. The five banner rows and the nine-cell OPS wall were not merely superseded - they were UNREACHABLE in production. THREE TOOLS WERE ALREADY LOST. RACK MAP, SOPS and BURNDOWN had no other reachable door. SOPS and BURNDOWN had exactly ONE caller each in the entire file and it was the ops-cell inside that hidden container; RACK MAP's only other route was a conditional Command stat tile. Measured at 390 on phone-webkit against live .463: zero reachable doors for those three, against one each for the six that also sit in the Command Field tools row. A technician could not open SOPs or Burndown at all. SO THE FOLD WAS A RESTORE-THEN-DELETE, NEVER A DELETE. The three were added to the Field tools row FIRST, taking it from six to nine, and only then was the stack removed. Deleting first would have removed two tools from the product permanently. The row is in DEPLOY_TOOLS registry order, which is the same order the retired 3x3 wall used, so the layout a technician already learned survives the move - and 03-tools asserts that order with an order-sensitive comparison. Art is the same assets the retired cells used and was already in PRECACHE_URLS, so nothing was orphaned and the precache list did not move. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. #work-grid and #wk-job-host stay: wk_renderJob writes into the job host and wk_showGrid is still the BACK target from an open ops tool. The .bnr, .opsrow and .opswall CSS stays: it is inert, and its .rf-cname, .rf-cmeta and .chev neighbours are SHARED - the new PASTE row uses all three - so tidying there would risk a live door to delete bytes that cost nothing. wk_toggleOpsWall and wk_paintOpsWall stay, inert with zero callers; deleting them cascades into nine per-tool stat readers for no user benefit. THE PINNED TEST STAYS RED, ON PURPOSE. 03-tools has carried an expected-failure since v1.14.385 asserting that the ops tools are one tap from the BUILD landing, quoting the wall's own shipped promise. The Field tools row lives in #pg-cmd - Command, not Build - so every tool is reachable again but Contract A7's operational-centre claim is still unmet. The pin was updated to name the new cause and was NOT repointed at Command, because repointing it would be weakening a test to fit the code, which that block's own header forbids. It flips when Build has a door. CREDIT WHERE IT IS DUE: the harness found this first. The bw-on cause, the exact CSS rule and the hidden wall were already written into that pinned test months ago. VERIFIED on phone-webkit, each spec alone: 44-tool-reachability 3, 03-tools 28, 43-paste-door 12, 01-nav 14, 02-build-forge 14, 06-composition 12, 42-paste-classifier 6 - 89 passed. Gates: three-stamp lockstep at .464, phantom-guard exit 0, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, 0 bare LF, 0 mojibake. DEVICE-VERIFY: open COMMAND and scroll to Field tools - nine tiles, and SOPs and Burndown open. Open BUILD - the old five-row banner stack and its 3x3 tool wall are gone.
